description: Add Lama Cleaner inpainting integration - a pipeline step that sends the image + text region masks to a Lama Cleaner endpoint to produce a cleaned version of the manga page (text removed). The cleanedImageBase64 field already exists in the PipelineResponse type.
steps: Step 1 - Backend provider: Create backend/app/providers/lama_cleaner.py. Implement an async function inpaint(image_bytes: bytes, mask_bytes: bytes, lama_url: str) -> bytes that POSTs to {lama_url}/inpaint with multipart form data (image file + mask file). The mask should be a binary image where white = areas to inpaint (text regions). Return the cleaned image bytes. Include retry logic and error classification.

Step 2 - Backend schemas: Add inpainting-related fields to PipelineRequest or a new InpaintConfig model in backend/app/schemas/pipeline.py: InpaintConfig with enabled: bool, lama_url: str (default 'http://localhost:8080').

Step 3 - Backend pipeline service: Update backend/app/services/pipeline.py to optionally run the Lama Cleaner inpainting step. After OCR produces bubbles with bounding boxes, generate a mask image (white rectangles at each bubble's bounding box coordinates on a black background) and call lama_cleaner.inpaint(). Set cleaned_image_b64 in the response. This runs as an alternative to the Torii cleaner. Import pillow or use a pure-python approach to generate the mask.
Step 4 - Backend requirements: Add 'Pillow' to backend/requirements.txt (needed for mask generation).
Step 5 - Backend deps: Add lama_url field to Byok or pass it through the pipeline request's inpaint config. Add X-Lama-Url header extraction to deps.py for user-configurable URL override.
Step 6 - Frontend types: No change needed - cleanedImageBase64 already exists in PipelineResponse.
Step 7 - Frontend store: Add inpaintEnabled (boolean, default false) and lamaCleanerUrl (string, default 'http://localhost:8080') to useTranslatorStore.ts with setters.
Step 8 - Frontend API client: Add X-Lama-Url header to byokHeaders() when lamaCleanerUrl is configured.

Step 9 - Frontend pipeline: Update pipelineApi.ts PipelineRequest type to include inpaint?: { enabled: boolean; lamaUrl?: string }. Update useTranslatePipeline.ts to pass inpaint config in the pipeline request when enabled.

Step 10 - Frontend settings: Add an 'Inpainting' section to the SettingsPanel (features/settings/SettingsPanel.tsx) with a toggle for enabling inpainting and a text input for the Lama Cleaner URL. Alternatively, create a small InpaintSettingsSection component.

Step 11 - Frontend App.tsx: Add the inpainting toggle to the sidebar (near the Torii cleaning toggle) with a paint brush icon. When inpainting is enabled and Torii cleaning is also enabled, show a warning that only one can be active (prefer inpainting or let user choose).
acceptance_criteria: InpaintConfig model exists in backend schemas
Pipeline service generates mask from bounding boxes and calls Lama Cleaner when enabled
Frontend has toggle for inpainting in sidebar/settings
Frontend sends inpaint config in pipeline request
